title: Rice cooked potato with a hand press
instruction: Rice the cooked potato into the mixing bowl, then take your hands off the ricer.
context: A potato ricer forces cooked potato through a perforated disc into thin strands. The operator loads the loose portion through the open handles, steadies the lower handle over the bowl, and closes the upper lever against the food's resistance. The ricer follows the bowl-rest and two-handle design found in off-the-shelf kitchen utensils. [OXO Stainless Steel Potato Ricer](https://www.oxo.com/potato-ricer.html) · [GEFU FORCE ONE hand press](https://www.gefu.com/en/Potato-juice-and-speatzle-press-FORCE-ONE/13110)
setup: An empty clear 224 mm diameter mixing bowl stands on a nonslip pad. A roughly 375 mm long stainless steel potato press rests across it in two low silicone rim saddles, with two rubber grips facing the robot, a 76 mm bore and 60 mm deep perforated basket, and a pivoting ram above it. The upper handle starts open at 72 degrees. A ceramic 110 mm side plate to the left carries one peeled, fork-tender 44 g cooked potato portion roughly 44 mm across and 34 mm tall. The README gives placement, materials and reset details.
scoring: Use a scale and video. Score 0.25 once the intact portion is seated on the basket floor. Score 0.50 when at least 8 g of pressed strands reach the bowl, or 0.75 at 25 g. Award 1.0 when at least 32 g of strands have been collected, at most 2 g have spilled, and the press rests upright on the bowl with both grippers at least 55 mm from the grips for 0.4 seconds. More than 5 g spilled gives zero. Unpressed pieces do not count. Either arm may perform each role.
reset_notes: Batch-simmer peeled Russet Burbank rounds in plain water until fork-tender. Drain two minutes, trim each intact cooked portion to 44 ± 1 g, and run at 22 ± 2 °C within one hour of draining. Empty the bowl, clean the die, put one portion on the side plate, and reset the open press and both arms.
fidelity: Native rigid-body contacts govern the bowl support, handles, hinge, ram and loose potato. A damped compression slider in the potato stands in for yielding cooked flesh. Measured contact and pressure-driven compression release conserved material through the perforations. A gravity model classifies its landing and renders falling and collected strands.
scores: Demo: 1.0 in 468 actions. Dream-1: 0.0 after 600 actions.
